I study behavioral treatments for depression and the measurement that makes them testable. Three threads — a longitudinal thesis on mindfulness-based behavioral activation, a systematic review of trans behavioral health care outcomes, and EEG research on stress and cannabis — share one method: reproducible data work in R, so every number here regenerates from data, not from memory.

## Master's Thesis

**The effectiveness of a brief, mindfulness-based behavioral activation intervention for college students with depression.** New Mexico Highlands University, M.S. Clinical Psychology. Advisor: Dr. David Pan.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Question** | Does a brief, outdoor mindfulness-based behavioral activation intervention reduce depressive symptoms in college students? |
| **Design** | Longitudinal; psychometrics and statistical analysis in R |
| **Status** | Data collection and analysis complete; manuscript in progress |
| **Advisor** | Dr. David Pan |

The full analysis pipeline — cleaning, psychometrics, longitudinal models, and automated reporting in Quarto — regenerates every table and figure from raw data. A public synthetic/de-identified demo is in preparation; no participant data will ever be published.

## Methods & Tools

- **R** — psychometrics, longitudinal analysis, visualization; reproducible reporting with Quarto
- **Assessment** — neuropsychological, cognitive, and intelligence testing in clinical intake and treatment-planning settings
- **Survey & data** — SPSS, Qualtrics
- **EEG** — acquisition and lab management (Heflin lab)
